$comment: Every third-party component a release archive actually contains.
One list, read by three tools: tools/write-sbom.ps1 builds the SPDX document from it,
tools/write-third-party-notices.ps1 assembles THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES from it, and
tools/publication-audit.ps1 checks that each entry still has its notice text. A component
added to the build and not added here fails the audit rather than shipping unattributed.
Where a package ships no licence file of its own, the notice under third-party/notices holds
the canonical text for its declared SPDX identifier, with the copyright line taken from the
package's own metadata. The authoritative text is always the upstream project's.

packages.name: BouncyCastle.Cryptography
packages.noticeSource: verbatim from the package's own LICENSE.md

packages.name: SharpCompress
packages.noticeSource: MIT text with the copyright line from package metadata; the package ships no licence file

packages.name: StbImageSharp
packages.noticeSource: Unlicense text; the package ships no licence file and declares a dual licence

packages.name: ZXingCpp
packages.purpose: QR detection and decoding; ships native assets for six runtime identifiers
packages.noticeSource: attribution pointing at the Apache-2.0 text shipped as LICENSE

vendored.name: erasure16-dotnet
vendored.purpose: systematic Cauchy Reed-Solomon over GF(2^16), vendored as source
vendored.noticeSource: carries its upstream NOTICE beside the source, staged as NOTICE.codecs

vendored.name: ldpc-staircase-dotnet
vendored.purpose: systematic LDPC-Staircase over GF(2), vendored as source; implements the RFC 5170 profile
vendored.noticeSource: carries its upstream NOTICE beside the source, staged as NOTICE.codecs
